The README says to turn detailed output on by default while keeping three things working: explicit plain/detailed overrides, counts, and successful empty-batch reports (README:12-13). It also says empty batches are valid in either mode and produce only `Items: 0` (README:9-10). The selector is staged (`git diff --cached`) and the candidate is the index. The worktree copies of `config.py` and `tests/test_report.py` match the index (parent-attested; the diff hunks match the files I read). No task scope was supplied.

  The call path is `app.report` (app.py:6-10) → `stats.summarize` (stats.py:1-5) → `formatting.format_summary` (formatting.py:5-9). `app.py:1` binds `DETAILED_REPORT` once at import. A grep found no other consumers outside `plugins/`.

  ### P1 - High
  
  - **[/tmp/fr-advisory-bootstrap-20261018/claude-candidate-R6M-isolated-1/stats.py:4]** (triggered by `config.py:1`) Turning detailed on by default makes empty-batch reports raise `ZeroDivisionError`
    - Profile: python · Checklist: code-quality-checklist.md (Boundary Conditions: division by zero / empty collections)
    - Triggered by: content — .py extension: config.py, tests/test_report.py
    - **Trigger and path:** Call `report([])` with no explicit mode. `app.py:7-8` resolves `detailed = DETAILED_REPORT`, which is now `True` (`config.py:1`). `summarize([], detailed=True)` then runs `sum([]) / len([])`, which is `0 / 0`.
    - **Expected:** `"Items: 0"`. The README says empty batches are valid in either mode and that this increment must "Preserve ... successful empty-batch reports".
    - **Actual:** an unhandled `ZeroDivisionError` comes out of `report`.
    - **Consequence:** Any caller that relies on the default and passes an empty batch now crashes, even though it worked at the base. This is a regression introduced by the change and breaks an explicit acceptance requirement. The `detailed=True` empty case was already broken at the base; this change puts that broken path on the default route.
    - **Confidence:** 95%. The trace is three short pure functions with no other branches. Python semantics make `0/0` on ints raise `ZeroDivisionError`. The only uncertainty is that I did not run the code.
    - **Suggested fix:** In `stats.summarize`, compute the mean only for populated batches: `if detailed and values:`. `format_summary` already leaves out `; Mean:` when the `"mean"` key is absent (formatting.py:7), so empty batches will return `Items: 0` in both modes. Do not catch the exception in `report` instead, because the formatter is already built around an absent mean. Add tests `test_default_empty` (`report([]) == "Items: 0"`) and `test_detailed_empty` (`report([], detailed=True) == "Items: 0"`) so the README's empty-batch guarantee is checked in every mode.

The README defines the default as the "checked-in" setting, so this is not a contract violation and I have not raised it as a finding.
